properties.natural_language: Any block received from a network peer (EXT-PEER-NODE) MUST be independently validated against the applicable fork rules before acceptance, regardless of peer identity.
Blocks received from untrusted peers MUST have their block number verified before determining which rule set (pre-Berlin or post-Berlin) to apply for validation.
Blocks from peers claiming to be at the fork block MUST NOT be accepted without full consensus rule validation to prevent fork confusion attacks.
The network operating state (EXT-NETWORK) MUST provide a consistent view of the current block number to determine fork activation status.
EIP proposals submitted by authors (EXT-EIP-AUTHORS) MUST go through formal review before inclusion in the Berlin meta-specification.
EIP submissions MUST be validated against the eth1.0-specs repository specification before aggregation into the Berlin hardfork.
The authoritative list of EIPs included in Berlin MUST be sourced exclusively from eth1.0-specs/berlin.md; no other source shall be treated as canonical.
The Berlin fork block number MUST be defined and agreed upon in client implementations before any fork activation logic executes.
All major Ethereum clients MUST activate Berlin at the exact same block number to prevent network splits and consensus failures.
Node operators MUST upgrade their client software before the fork block to avoid isolation from the canonical chain.
The eth1.0-specs repository MUST remain the single authoritative source for Berlin specification to prevent conflicting client implementations.
After ACTION-ACTIVATE-BERLIN-RULES completes, the network MUST be in STATE-POST-BERLIN and all subsequent blocks MUST be validated under Berlin rules.
After ACTION-CHECK-FORK-STATUS, blocks MUST be routed to exactly one validation path: pre-Berlin rules if block_number < fork_block, or Berlin rules if block_number >= fork_block.
After validation, a block MUST be in exactly one of STATE-BLOCK-VALID or STATE-BLOCK-INVALID; no block may exist in an indeterminate validation state.
After ACTION-AGGREGATE-EIPS, the finalized Berlin specification MUST include the complete set of constituent EIPs as recorded in DATA-BERLIN-SPEC.
After ACTION-BEGIN-TRANSACTION, a snapshot of the main trie and all storage tries MUST exist, enabling rollback to the exact pre-transaction state.
After ACTION-COMMIT-TRANSACTION, all state modifications made since the snapshot MUST be permanent at the current nesting level and the snapshot MUST be removed.
After ACTION-ROLLBACK-TRANSACTION, the state MUST be identical to the state at the time of the corresponding ACTION-BEGIN-TRANSACTION, discarding all intermediate modifications.
Nested transaction snapshots MUST form a proper stack: each commit or rollback removes exactly the most recent snapshot.
After ACTION-SET-ACCOUNT with a valid account value, the address MUST transition to STATE-ACCOUNT-EXISTS with the stored nonce, balance, code, and storage root.
After ACTION-DESTROY-ACCOUNT, the account and all associated storage MUST be removed, returning the address to STATE-ACCOUNT-NONEXISTENT.
After ACTION-MODIFY-STATE, if the resulting account has zero nonce, empty code, and zero balance, the account MUST be auto-destroyed per EIP-161.
After ACTION-GET-ACCOUNT on a nonexistent address, the return value MUST be EMPTY_ACCOUNT (zero nonce, zero balance, empty code).
After ACTION-SET-STORAGE with a non-zero value, the storage slot MUST transition to STATE-STORAGE-SLOT-SET with the written value.
After ACTION-SET-STORAGE with value U256(0), the storage slot MUST be deleted, transitioning to STATE-STORAGE-SLOT-EMPTY.
Before ACTION-SET-STORAGE, the account MUST be verified to exist via ACTION-ASSERT-ACCOUNT-EXISTS; storage writes to nonexistent accounts are invalid.
After ACTION-DESTROY-STORAGE, all storage slots for the address MUST be removed, leaving STATE-STORAGE-DESTROYED.
After ACTION-SET-TRANSIENT (TSTORE), the value MUST be retrievable via ACTION-GET-TRANSIENT (TLOAD) within the same transaction.
Transient storage MUST be cleared at transaction end; no transient values may persist across transaction boundaries.
For accounts created in the current transaction, ACTION-GET-STORAGE-ORIGINAL MUST return U256(0) for all storage slots, as no pre-existing storage exists.
Transaction snapshot nesting depth is bounded only by available memory and call stack depth; no explicit maximum nesting limit is enforced.
Trie operations MUST be atomic and consistent within a single thread of execution; concurrent modifications are not permitted.
The modify_state function MUST always check for and auto-destroy empty accounts after modification, ensuring EIP-161 compliance.
State root calculations MUST only be performed when no transaction snapshots are active, to ensure consistency.
Block producer (EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER) MUST correctly compute the reserve price using parent block data; the computed value is validated by all nodes independently.
Reserve price calculations from block producers MUST use authentic parent block base_fee_per_gas; manipulated parent data would produce invalid blocks rejected by validators.
Blocks received from peers for validation MUST have their excess_blob_gas recomputed locally using the modified calc_excess_blob_gas with reserve price logic.
After ACTION-COMPARE-FEES, the system MUST be in exactly one of STATE-NORMAL-PRICING-MODE or STATE-RESERVE-PRICING-MODE.
After ACTION-CHECK-RESERVE-CONDITION evaluates true, the excess blob gas MUST be calculated using the reserve mode formula: excess += blob_gas_used * (max - target) / max.
After ACTION-CHECK-RESERVE-CONDITION evaluates false, the excess blob gas MUST be calculated using the normal formula: excess += blob_gas_used - target_blob_gas.
After ACTION-LOAD-BLOB-SCHEDULE at fork activation, the new target and max blob gas parameters from EIP-7840 MUST be immediately active for the current block.
After ACTION-COMPARE-HEADER, if the recalculated excess_blob_gas matches the header, the block MUST be in STATE-BLOCK-VALID; otherwise STATE-BLOCK-INVALID.
The blob base fee MUST never fall below the reserve price floor defined as BLOB_BASE_COST * base_fee_per_gas / GAS_PER_BLOB when the reserve condition is active.
The reserve price check MUST be evaluated every block, enabling smooth transitions between normal and reserve pricing modes.
The blobSchedule parameters 'max' and 'target' MUST correspond to MAX_BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOCK and TARGET_BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOCK from EIP-7840.
The ratio BLOB_BASE_COST / GAS_PER_BLOB (1/16) MUST represent an appropriate minimum ratio between blob and execution costs to prevent economic distortion.
All clients MUST implement identical conditional excess_blob_gas calculation with reserve price logic to prevent consensus failures.
The EIP-7840 blobSchedule mechanism MUST provide valid target and max parameters before reserve price calculation executes.
Attackers MUST NOT be able to manipulate execution gas prices to artificially inflate or deflate blob costs via the reserve price mechanism.
Input from calling contracts (EXT-CONTRACT-CALLER) to alt_bn128 precompiles MUST be fully validated for length and curve membership before execution.
Untrusted caller input (EXT-UNTRUSTED-INPUT) MUST pass input length validation before any curve point validation occurs.
After ACTION-IDENTIFY-PRECOMPILE, exactly one of ECADD (0x06), ECMUL (0x07), or Pairing (0x08) MUST be selected based on the target address.
After ACTION-COMPUTE-ECADD-GAS, the gas cost MUST be exactly 150 gas (reduced from 500).
After ACTION-COMPUTE-ECMUL-GAS, the gas cost MUST be exactly 6,000 gas (reduced from 40,000).
After ACTION-COMPUTE-PAIRING-GAS, the gas cost MUST be exactly 34,000*k + 45,000 where k is the number of pairings.
After ACTION-DEDUCT-GAS with sufficient gas, execution MUST proceed to STATE-GAS-DEDUCTED; with insufficient gas, execution MUST halt at STATE-OUT-OF-GAS.
After ACTION-VALIDATE-INPUT-LENGTH, input with incorrect length MUST transition to STATE-LENGTH-INVALID and the precompile MUST fail.
After ACTION-VALIDATE-POINT-ON-CURVE, points not satisfying the alt_bn128 curve equation MUST be rejected at STATE-POINT-INVALID.
After ACTION-RETURN-RESULT, the precompile result (point coordinates or boolean) MUST be returned to the calling context and EVM execution MUST resume.
Gas cost changes from EIP-1108 MUST only apply to blocks after the Istanbul fork; historical blocks use the original costs (500, 40000, 80000k+100000).
The reduced gas costs MUST still prevent DoS attacks; the pricing baseline assumes 25.86 gas per microsecond relative to ecrecover at 3,000 gas.
The benchmarked performance baseline (25.86 gas/microsecond) MUST hold across all client implementations to prevent DoS on slower clients.
Adversarially-chosen inputs MUST NOT cause worst-case execution times significantly exceeding average case for any precompile operation.
All client implementations MUST produce identical results for the same alt_bn128 precompile inputs to prevent consensus failures.
Data from untrusted external sources (EXT-UNTRUSTED-SOURCE) MUST be hashed before being used as an integrity identifier; raw untrusted data MUST NOT be used directly as a key or identifier.
Untrusted data MUST have its integrity verified via hash comparison (ACTION-COMPARE-HASHES) before being accepted as authentic.
After ACTION-COMPUTE-DIGEST, the output MUST be exactly 32 bytes (256 bits) represented as Hash32.
After ACTION-COMPUTE-DIGEST512, the output MUST be exactly 64 bytes (512 bits) represented as Hash64.
After ACTION-COMPARE-HASHES, if hashes match, the system MUST transition to STATE-INTEGRITY-VERIFIED; if they differ, to STATE-INTEGRITY-FAILED.
The keccak256 and keccak512 hash functions MUST be deterministic: identical inputs MUST always produce identical outputs across all invocations and implementations.
Hash functions MUST accept any valid bytes/bytearray input without length limits; the Keccak sponge construction handles arbitrary-length inputs.
Hash functions MUST be pure computations that do not raise exceptions for valid byte inputs.
The underlying Keccak cryptographic primitive MUST be correctly implemented; a compromised implementation would enable collision attacks and transaction forgery.
Finding Keccak256 or Keccak512 collisions MUST remain computationally infeasible; practical collisions would enable replay attacks and state root forgery.
Transactions from external submitters (EXT-TX-SUBMITTER) MUST have their type byte validated against the set of known types (0-4) before any further processing.
After ACTION-CHECK-TX-TYPE with an unknown type byte, the system MUST raise TransactionTypeError and transition to STATE-TX-TYPE-ERROR.
After ACTION-CHECK-CONTRACT-CREATION with a disallowed type (e.g., blob transactions), the system MUST raise TransactionTypeContractCreationError.
After ACTION-CHECK-FEE-STRUCTURE with maxFeePerGas < baseFeePerGas, the system MUST reject the transaction with STATE-INSUFFICIENT-MAX-FEE.
After ACTION-CHECK-FEE-STRUCTURE with maxPriorityFeePerGas > maxFeePerGas, the system MUST reject with STATE-PRIORITY-FEE-ERROR.
After ACTION-CHECK-BLOB-DATA-EXISTS with no blobs, the system MUST reject the transaction with STATE-NO-BLOB-DATA.
After ACTION-CHECK-BLOB-VERSIONED-HASH with invalid version byte, the system MUST reject with STATE-INVALID-VERSIONED-HASH.
After ACTION-CHECK-BLOB-GAS-LIMIT with blob gas exceeding block maximum, the system MUST reject with STATE-BLOB-GAS-EXCEEDED.
After ACTION-CHECK-BLOB-FEE with maxFeePerBlobGas below current blob base fee, the system MUST reject with STATE-INSUFFICIENT-BLOB-FEE.
After ACTION-CHECK-INIT-CODE-SIZE with code exceeding MAX_INITCODE_SIZE, the system MUST reject with STATE-INIT-CODE-TOO-LARGE.
After ACTION-CHECK-AUTH-LIST with an empty authorization list, the system MUST reject with STATE-EMPTY-AUTH-LIST-ERROR.
Valid transaction type bytes MUST be exactly {0, 1, 2, 3, 4} in Prague fork; any other type byte triggers TransactionTypeError.
Blob transactions (type 3) MUST NOT be permitted to create contracts; type 4 authorization transactions may also have creation restrictions.
Exception handlers MUST be invoked correctly and MUST NOT be bypassed; all invalid transactions MUST be rejected through the proper exception path.
The block base fee MUST be correctly propagated from the parent block header before fee validation occurs.
Wire protocol messages from network peers (EXT-PEER-NODE) MUST be validated for correct message type code before processing.
Messages from untrusted peers MUST be checked for deprecated message types (0x0d GetNodeData, 0x0e NodeData) and rejected if the client runs eth/67.
After ACTION-UPGRADE-PROTOCOL from eth/66 to eth/67, GetNodeData (0x0d) and NodeData (0x0e) message types MUST be disabled.
After ACTION-CHECK-MESSAGE-TYPE identifies a deprecated message, ACTION-REJECT-DEPRECATED-MESSAGE MUST be invoked; the message MUST NOT be processed.
After ACTION-CHECK-PROTOCOL-VERSION determines peer supports only eth/67, state retrieval MUST use snap protocol (GetByteCodes or GetTrieNodes) instead of GetNodeData.
An eth/67 client receiving deprecated GetNodeData requests MUST either ignore the message or disconnect the peer; it MUST NOT process the request.
eth/66 support MUST be maintained during the transition period until network-wide adoption of eth/67 is sufficient.
Clients upgrading to eth/67 MUST have snap protocol support implemented before the upgrade to maintain state sync capability.
Sufficient eth/66 or snap-capable peers MUST exist in the network during the transition period to enable state synchronization for all nodes.
The removal of GetNodeData MUST NOT introduce new attack vectors compared to the snap protocol replacement.
After ACTION-BLOCKHASH-EXECUTE with a block in valid range (within 256 blocks, not current or future), the correct block hash MUST be pushed to the stack.
After ACTION-BLOCKHASH-EXECUTE with a block out of range (>256 blocks ago, current, or future), zero MUST be pushed to the stack.
After each block environment opcode (COINBASE, TIMESTAMP, NUMBER, PREVRANDAO, GASLIMIT, CHAINID) executes, the corresponding value MUST be pushed to the stack and PC incremented.
After ACTION-CHARGE-GAS-BLOCKHASH, exactly 20 gas MUST be deducted; after ACTION-CHARGE-GAS-BASE, exactly 2 gas MUST be deducted.
After gas charge with insufficient gas for any block opcode, execution MUST halt with STATE-OUT-OF-GAS (OutOfGasError).
After ACTION-VALIDATE-STACK-BLOCKHASH with an empty stack, the system MUST transition to STATE-STACK-UNDERFLOW.
After stack validation with a full stack (1024 elements), any push operation MUST transition to STATE-STACK-OVERFLOW.
PREVRANDAO provides beacon chain randomness that MAY be predictable by validators; contracts MUST NOT rely on it as sole entropy source for high-value outcomes.
TIMESTAMP values can vary within protocol-defined bounds (~15 seconds tolerance); contracts using time-dependent logic MUST account for this tolerance.
block_env MUST be populated with correct, validated block data before EVM execution begins; all block opcodes read from this pre-populated environment.
Block proposers MUST NOT be able to manipulate PREVRANDAO beyond their natural ability to observe the value before others.
Attackers MUST NOT be able to forge block hashes in the recent 256-block window; BLOCKHASH-based commit-reveal schemes depend on this property.
Transactions from external submitters (EXT-TX-SUBMITTER) MUST trigger access list initialization that includes the COINBASE address as warm before EVM execution.
After ACTION-ADD-COINBASE, the COINBASE address MUST be present in accessed_addresses, ensuring warm access costs for any subsequent COINBASE interaction.
After access list initialization completes, accessed_addresses MUST contain sender, recipient, all precompile addresses, and COINBASE.
After ACTION-CHECK-ACCESS-LIST post-EIP-3651, COINBASE lookups MUST return warm status, resulting in ~100 gas access cost instead of ~2600.
After ACTION-CALL-WITH-VALUE to COINBASE, ETH MUST be transferred to the block builder with warm access gas costs (~2500 gas savings vs cold).
COINBASE warming MUST apply uniformly to all transaction types (legacy, EIP-2930, EIP-1559, EIP-4844, EIP-7702) since EIP-2929 access lists are universal.
COINBASE MUST be added to accessed_addresses during the same initialization phase as sender, recipient, and precompiles, before any EVM execution begins.
The COINBASE address MUST be known from the block header at transaction execution start for warm initialization to succeed.
MEV protocols and block builder payment contracts benefit from warm COINBASE only if builders use their declared COINBASE address for reward receipt.
EIP-2929 access list gas accounting MUST be identically implemented across all clients for correct warm/cold cost differentiation.
Withdrawals from the consensus layer (EXT-CONSENSUS-LAYER) MUST be validated through consensus mechanisms and authenticated via Engine API JWT before execution layer processing.
Withdrawal data (validator index, address, amount) from the consensus layer MUST have its integrity verified via withdrawals_root commitment before applying balance changes.
Block header from block proposer (EXT-BLOCK-PROPOSER) MUST contain a withdrawals_root field that can be independently verified against the withdrawal list.
Withdrawal list in execution payload from block proposer MUST be verifiable against the committed withdrawals_root in the header.
Validator withdrawal requests (EXT-CONSENSUS-VALIDATOR) MUST be validated by the consensus layer before the execution layer sees them.
After ACTION-APPLY-WITHDRAWAL, the recipient address balance MUST be unconditionally increased by the withdrawal amount in wei, regardless of account type.
After ACTION-CONVERT-GWEI-TO-WEI, the amount MUST be correctly converted from Gwei (uint64) to Wei for the balance update.
After ACTION-COMPUTE-TRIE-ROOT, the computed Merkle-Patricia trie root MUST be deterministically derived from the indexed withdrawal data.
After ACTION-VERIFY-ROOT-MATCH, if computed root matches the header, STATE-ROOT-VERIFIED MUST be reached; if mismatch, STATE-VALIDATION-FAILED and the block MUST be rejected.
After ACTION-PROCESS-NO-GAS, the withdrawal balance update MUST complete without consuming any gas.
Withdrawal processing MUST be gas-free and MUST NOT fail; balance updates are unconditional system-level operations.
Withdrawal indices MUST be monotonically increasing and never duplicated across all blocks.
Withdrawal balance credits MUST be unconditionally applied regardless of whether the recipient address is an EOA or a contract.
The empty list in serialization RLP([transactions, [], withdrawals]) MUST be preserved as a placeholder; it MUST NOT affect withdrawal processing.
Consensus layer validation of withdrawals MUST be correct and complete before passing to execution layer; bypassed validation could credit arbitrary amounts.
Engine API MUST correctly transmit withdrawal data between consensus and execution clients without data loss or corruption.
The bounded quantity of withdrawals per block MUST be sufficient to process validator exits in reasonable time to prevent unbounded queue growth.
